name: Helicopter
title: Helicopter (drive train and rotor controls)
intro: This is a light helicopter. Explode it (🧩) to see the turboshaft engine, main gearbox, swashplate, teetering rotor and tail rotor. Ask me "How does a helicopter fly forward?"
suggest: How does a helicopter fly forward?
Why does it need a tail rotor?
Open the doors and look inside?

engine.name: Turboshaft engine
engine.info: The helicopter's heart. It draws in air, compresses it and burns it with fuel; the hot gas spins a turbine, and a shaft sends the power forward. A window shows the turbine inside.

turbine.name: Power turbine
turbine.info: Spun at high speed by the hot gas from combustion. Every turning part of the helicopter starts here.

input_shaft.name: Input shaft
input_shaft.info: Carries the engine's rotation into the main gearbox. It spins very fast but with little force.

main_gearbox.name: Main gearbox
main_gearbox.info: Reduces the engine's tens of thousands of rpm to a few hundred rpm at the main rotor, multiplying the force many times. A quarter of the case is cut away to show the gears.

bevel_gear.name: Bevel gear and sun gear
bevel_gear.info: The 71-tooth bevel gear turns the horizontal input into vertical rotation; the sun gear above it drives the planet gears.

planets.name: Planet gears
planets.info: They orbit the sun gear while rolling inside the fixed outer ring gear, reducing the speed again and handing it to the planet carrier and the mast.

mast.name: Mast and planet carrier
mast.info: The main shaft rising out of the gearbox, with the rotor on top. It turns about 15 times slower than the input shaft, with about 15 times the force.

rotor_hub.name: Rotor hub (teetering)
rotor_hub.info: The two blades sit on a central pivot like a seesaw: when one rises the other drops, so the whole rotor disc can tilt.

blade_1.name: Blade 1
blade_1.info: Like a wing going round in a circle. Raise its leading edge a little (more pitch) and it pushes more air down, making more lift.

blade_2.name: Blade 2
blade_2.info: Turns together with the other blade. Each blade can twist about its own long axis to change its pitch.

swashplate_lower.name: Lower swashplate (fixed)
swashplate_lower.info: Held up by three servos, it can rise and fall as a whole or tilt in any direction, but it doesn't turn. The pilot's commands enter the spinning parts here.

swashplate_upper.name: Upper swashplate (rotating)
swashplate_upper.info: Turns with the rotor but rises and tilts together with the lower plate, twisting the blades through the pitch links.

pitch_link_1.name: Pitch link 1
pitch_link_1.info: Passes the upper swashplate's height to the blade's pitch horn: link up, leading edge up.

pitch_link_2.name: Pitch link 2
pitch_link_2.info: The other pitch link, controlling the other blade.

scissors.name: Scissor link
scissors.info: Connects the upper swashplate to the mast, so the plate turns with the rotor while still free to rise and tilt.

servo_1.name: Servo 1 (front)
servo_1.info: A hydraulic servo pushing one point of the lower swashplate. All three pushing together raise or lower it (collective); pushing differently tilts it (cyclic).

servo_2.name: Servo 2 (left rear)
servo_2.info: A hydraulic servo pushing one point of the lower swashplate. All three pushing together raise or lower it (collective); pushing differently tilts it (cyclic).

servo_3.name: Servo 3 (right rear)
servo_3.info: A hydraulic servo pushing one point of the lower swashplate. All three pushing together raise or lower it (collective); pushing differently tilts it (cyclic).

tail_driveshaft.name: Tail driveshaft
tail_driveshaft.info: The long shaft running from the main gearbox all the way to the tail, driving the tail rotor.

tail_gearbox.name: Tail gearbox
tail_gearbox.info: Turns the drive 90° at the tail and hands the shaft's rotation to the tail rotor.

tail_rotor.name: Tail rotor
tail_rotor.info: As the main rotor turns one way, the reaction twists the body the other way. The tail rotor pushes sideways to hold the body straight; the pedals change its pitch to turn the nose left and right.

cyclic.name: Cyclic stick
cyclic.info: The stick in the pilot's right hand. Push it any way and the swashplate tilts that way, the rotor disc follows, and the helicopter flies in that direction.

collective.name: Collective lever
collective.info: The lever by the pilot's left hand. Raise it and both blades' pitch increases together: more lift, and the helicopter climbs.

pedals.name: Anti-torque pedals
pedals.info: Press left or right to change the tail rotor's pitch and turn the nose left or right.

control_rods.name: Control rods
control_rods.info: Connect the pilot's stick, lever and pedals to the servos and the tail rotor.

fuel_tank.name: Fuel tank
fuel_tank.info: Holds the fuel, in the middle of the body near the centre of gravity, so the balance doesn't change as the fuel is used.

skids.name: Skids
skids.info: Landing gear made of two tubes: lighter and simpler than wheels.

fuselage.name: Fuselage
fuselage.info: The helicopter's main body, with the cockpit, seats and instrument panel at the front. Explode it (🧩) to see the engine and gearbox above and the controls below.

canopy.name: Canopy
canopy.info: The clear cover over the front and top of the cockpit, so the pilot can see forward and down.

door_l.name: Left front door
door_l.info: The door beside the pilot's seat. Hinged at the front edge, it opens outwards.

door_r.name: Right front door
door_r.info: Hinged at the front edge, it opens outwards.

rear_door_l.name: Left rear door
rear_door_l.info: The back-seat door, hinged at the rear edge, opening outwards.

rear_door_r.name: Right rear door
rear_door_r.info: The back-seat door, hinged at the rear edge, opening outwards.

transmission_cowling.name: Transmission cowling
transmission_cowling.info: The cover over the main gearbox and the lower swashplate, so the air flows past smoothly.

engine_cowling.name: Engine cowling
engine_cowling.info: The cover over the turboshaft engine, with the exhaust at the back.

tail_boom.name: Tail boom
tail_boom.info: The long boom reaching back from the body, with the tail rotor's driveshaft running inside. The further back the tail rotor, the less force it needs to cancel the torque.

tail_fins.name: Tail fins
tail_fins.info: The vertical fin and the horizontal stabiliser. In forward flight they keep the body pointing straight ahead, like the feathers on an arrow.

drives.power: Power (turbine → gearbox → main rotor and tail rotor)

power.title: How the engine turns the rotor

steps.say: Hot gas in the turboshaft engine spins the turbine at tens of thousands of rpm.
The input shaft carries the rotation into the main gearbox, and the bevel gear turns it from horizontal to vertical.

quiz.q: The engine spins very fast. Why does the rotor turn so much slower?
options: The gearbox trades speed for force
Cutting the speed about 15 times multiplies the torque about 15 times: enough to turn the long, heavy blades.
The engine is deliberately throttled back
The engine is most efficient at high speed; the gearbox does the reducing.
Air resistance slows it
Drag has to be overcome, but the speed is set by the gear ratio.

steps.say: The planet gears reduce the speed once more, and the planet carrier turns the mast and the blades.
At the same time the tail driveshaft sends part of the power to the tail rotor.

quiz.q: What would happen without a tail rotor?
options: The body would spin the opposite way to the rotor
The engine pushes the rotor one way, and the rotor pushes the body the other way (torque reaction). The tail rotor pushes sideways to counter it.
It couldn't take off
Lift comes from the main rotor, so it could lift off, but the body would keep spinning.
Nothing
It would keep spinning. Only designs like coaxial twin rotors can do without a tail rotor.

steps.say: The pilot raises the collective lever, and the three servos push the lower swashplate up together.
The upper swashplate rises with it, and the pitch links raise the leading edges of both blades at once.

quiz.q: Raise the collective. What do the two blades do?
options: Both get more pitch, making more lift
Together they push a little more air down, and the helicopter climbs.
They spin faster
Rotor speed stays almost fixed; it's the pitch that changes.
One gets more, one less
That's the cyclic; the collective changes both together.

steps.say: More pitch also means more drag, so the engine has to give more power to keep the rotor from slowing down.
The pilot pushes the cyclic forward, and the servos tilt both swashplates forward together.
On every turn, each blade has more pitch on one side and less on the other.

quiz.q: Is the rotor disc highest where the blade pitch is greatest?
options: No, the high point comes 90° later
That's gyroscopic precession: a spinning rotor responds a quarter turn after the force is applied, so the maximum pitch has to come 90° early.
Yes, at the same spot
The rotor is spinning, so the response comes a quarter turn later.
The high point is on the opposite side
The difference is 90°, not 180°.

steps.say: The result: the rotor disc tilts forward, the lift leans forward, and the helicopter flies forward.

tail_shaft.title: Broken tail driveshaft
tail_shaft.short: The main rotor turns, the tail rotor has stopped
tail_shaft.symptom: The turbine is running and the main rotor turns normally, but the small rotor at the tail has stopped. In the air, the body would keep spinning round. What do you think is broken?
tail_shaft.hint: The tail rotor has no engine of its own. Where does its power come from, and what carries it all the way to the tail?
suspects: The tail rotor blades are broken
tail_shaft.cause: The driveshaft from the main gearbox to the tail has broken. The main rotor keeps turning, but the tail rotor gets no power.
tail_shaft.why: Why does the helicopter keep spinning when the tail driveshaft breaks?
tail_shaft.answer: As the main rotor turns, the reaction pushes the body the opposite way. The tail rotor, driven from the main gearbox by the tail driveshaft, pushes sideways to cancel that torque. With the shaft broken the tail rotor stops, nothing cancels the torque, and the body spins.
